value.text: Kora confronts Nathaniel about killing her mother, Jiaying, but he wins her back with lies about Jiaying. When she lets Daisy go, he shoots her and has her locked up.

verdicts.why: Kora learns of Jiaying's death in S7#11 (May shows her the body and says she died protecting Daisy from Malick); in S7#12 she questions him and he wins her back. Fix is right, but 'lies about her' leaves the second 'her' unclear, so it names Jiaying.

In S7#12 Malick argues with Sibyl to let him kill the agents; she says Daisy reaching Simmons raises the odds of finding Fitz and tells him not to interfere. He then tells Kora they must finish Daisy whatever Sibyl says, and Kora goes after her. Nothing about leaving Quake to the Hunters.
In S7#12 Fitz only arrives at the end, dropping through the Quantum Realm portal at Krazy Kanoe in 1983. Helping finish the Chronicom mission is S7#13.

In Loki S2#1 O.B. sends Mobius to the Loom with the Temporal Aura Extractor to pull Loki out, then seals the Loom behind blast doors. The Loom is never saved (it fails in S2#4 and Loki destroys it in S2#6), so 'save the Loom' is false.

X-5 brushing Mobius off over the jet ski photos is S2#1. In S2#2 Mobius corners Wolfe at the 1977 premiere asking about a sequel, Loki blocks him, and in holding Wolfe mocks Mobius for not knowing who he was a variant of until Mobius slaps him. Since they first deal with each other in S2#1, that title may also deserve its own stage.

The hunt, the Lamentis-1 capture and Mobius's pruning are S1#2 to S1#4. In S1#5 Mobius rescues Sylvie from Alioth in a car, apologizes for what the TVA did to her as a child, backs her plan over Loki's, and leaves for the TVA with the TemPad she gives him.

value.title: Loki S1#4
value.text: Mobius hunts the Variant who has been attacking the TVA, and when she and Loki set off a Nexus Event on Lamentis-1, he sends Timedoors to bring them in.
value.on_a_card_about_b: The Variant Mobius hunts and has brought in from Lamentis-1.
value.on_b_card_about_a: The TVA agent who hunts Sylvie and has her captured.

verdicts.why: Once S1#5 keeps only its own events, the earlier hunt drops out of the connection. The rule that a connection starting in an earlier title gets a stage there settles it: in S1#4 Mobius spots the Nexus Event and sends Timedoors to Lamentis-1 to bring in Loki and the Variant.

value.text: Luke tracks down Turk Barrett, whose tip-off led to Pop's death, throws him into a dumpster and crushes it shut until Turk gives up Diamondback's warehouse.

verdicts.why: In S1#12 Luke confronts Turk over selling out Chico, which led to Pop's death, throws him into a dumpster and crushes it, trapping him until he gives up the warehouse. Turk is a Hell's Kitchen crook. The fix's 'crushes him' says Turk himself is crushed, so it is reworded. They first deal with each other in S1#2, when Luke orders Turk out of Pop's, which may also deserve a stage.

Shades does the killing, but it is not shown to be his own idea. In S1#8 Mariah agrees they would have to kill Candace if she talked, and in S2#12 Shades testifies that he killed Candace on Mariah's orders. 'Mariah has her killed' stands, and the stage is not earlier than anything it describes.
The Cottonmouth cover-up is S1#7 (stage 0). In S1#13 Shades uses Misty's phone to lure Candace out and kills her, Mariah is freed, and at the reopening of Harlem's Paradise she kisses him.

The concussion treatment is S2#4 (stage 0). In S2#7 Bushmaster sets the brownstone on fire with Mariah tied up and Tilda cut loose, Tilda tries to free Mariah, and Luke arrives and gets them both out.

In S2#12 Tilda tells Bushmaster her mother must be killed, tells him about the secret passageways into Harlem's Paradise and gives him a supershot of Nightshade. The current text sums up their whole arc instead.

Shades surrenders to Misty in S2#11. In S2#12 she sets up his testimony for full immunity, tells him the deal fails unless he gets Mariah's revolver, and he hands it over at Harlem's Paradise. She is not hunting him in this title.
In S2#13 D.W. confronts Luke at Pop's about acting as Harlem's new crime boss before Mariah dies and her will is read. Luke only gets Harlem's Paradise in the later will-reading scene.
Mabel taking Tilda away is the S2#8 reveal (stage 1). In S2#13 Tilda visits Mariah in jail, turns down starting over, and kisses her goodbye with poison on her lips, which kills Mariah.

The arrest line in the episode has no speaker labels, and the sources conflict: the episode page credits Misty, while the Ridley and Mariah pages say Ridley takes her in and tells her a court will convict her. With no error shown, the evidence rule keeps the stage.
In Market Forces (#4) Peter tries to ask Betty to the Fall Formal, but a Shocker tremor rattles the city and she never answers. She turns him down as too young in #6 (stage 1).

In The Uncertainty Principle (#9) the Goblin kidnaps Hammerhead and tries to recruit him, Hammerhead stays loyal to Tombstone, and the Goblin dangles him over molten metal as bait. It is Spider-Man, not Hammerhead, who accuses the Goblin of being Norman.

Harry is never really the Goblin: in #26 Norman says he found Harry passed out on Globulin Green and dressed him in the costume. In #9 Harry is found in the costume, collapses, and Norman takes him to Europe to recover.

value.text: Otto brings Marko into his Sinister Six. Electro frees Sandman from Ryker's Island as part of Otto's breakout, and Sandman fights Spider-Man under Otto's lead.

verdicts.why: The current text retells the #5 experiment (stage 0). In Group Therapy (#11) Electro shuts off the security on Sandman's cell and Ock leads the villains out to attack Spider-Man. The fix is right, but its 'he' could mean Electro, so it names Sandman.

value.text: Otto brings O'Hirn into his Sinister Six. Electro frees Rhino from Ryker's Island as part of Otto's breakout, and Rhino fights Spider-Man under Otto's lead.

verdicts.why: The current text retells the #6 bonding (stage 0). In Group Therapy (#11) Electro shuts off the security on Rhino's cell and Ock leads the villains out to attack Spider-Man. The fix is right, but its 'he' could mean Electro, so it names Rhino.
Calling the #11 team the 'first' Sinister Six points ahead to the Master Planner rebuilding it in Reinforcement (#16), a later title. Dropping 'first' leaves the rest true.
